For a Panasonic NN-H98 that isn't heating, there are two main possibilities: either it's set to a mode that doesn't use the microwave energy (like a grill-only or defrost setting), or there is a fault in the high-voltage heating circuit. To narrow this down, please try these owner-safe checks:
1. Ensure it is set to a standard microwave mode (e.g. Auto Cook or 100% Power) and not 'Grill', 'Combi' or a low power level.
2. Place a cup of water inside and run it for one minute on full power. Please tell me: did the water get hot, or is it still cold? And do you hear any abnormal buzzing or humming when it tries to heat?
its on microwave mode. water stops after about 10-15 secs with h98 on the screen and the water's still cold. not sure about any humming. also h98 is the code, the model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ

The H98 code on your Panasonic NN-CD87KSBPQ specifically indicates a fault with the high-voltage power circuit—most commonly the inverter board that drives the magnetron, or the magnetron itself. Because this appliance uses an inverter system (standard for Panasonic), and because the error code appears immediately while the water remains cold, the machine is detecting that it cannot generate microwave energy. This is a high-voltage fault involving lethal voltages stored in capacitors even when unplugged. It requires specialist testing and replacement of internal components by an engineer; there are no owner-safe fixes for this specific error code once settings have been confirmed correct. Please stop using the appliance to avoid further damage or safety risks. You will need to contact a qualified microwave repair technician or Panasonic support for a diagnosis and repair.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.

candidates: High-voltage circuit fault (magnetron, inverter board or HV components) (high)
